s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities, and specific histiocytic infiltrate pattern

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with skin lesions, diabetes insipidus, and growth retardation, although immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100

shortlist.label: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fits with clinical presentation of skin lesions and systemic involvement, and immunohistochemical results positive for CD68

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches skin lesions and systemic involvement, although less common than other differentials

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with histiocytic infiltrate and skin manifestations, although less common than other differentials

raw.rationale: The patient's skin lesions, which are reddish-brown papules, nodules, and plaques, along with the presence of a dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis and negative immunohistochemical results for CD1a and S-100, are consistent with Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma. Additionally, the patient's history of central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism can be associated with this condition.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester Disease
rejected.why: While Erdheim-Chester Disease can present with similar systemic symptoms, the skin biopsy findings and immunohistochemical results do not fully align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: The negative immunohistochemical results for CD1a and S-100 argue against Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis, which typically expresses these markers.

rejected.label: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: This is a broad category, and while the patient's condition could fall under this umbrella, the specific findings are more closely aligned with Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Rosai-Dorfman disease typically presents with lymphadenopathy and distinct histopathological features, such as emperipolesis, which are not described in this case.
